title: Nomes e Sobrenomes do Brasil (pt-BR)
subtitle: 47k given names and 27k surnames: CNPJ counts, IBGE Census data, GPT meanings
description:
**Nomes e sobrenomes do Brasil**: 47 mil nomes e 27 mil sobrenomes com frequência no cadastro CNPJ, dados do Censo 2010 do IBGE e significados escritos por GPT. **Brazilian given names and surnames** with CNPJ counts, IBGE 2010 Census data and meanings written by OpenAI models in 2023.

This is the database behind nomessobrenomes.com, a 90,000-page static site built by the author in 2023. It works two ways:

- **A list of Brazilian names with real frequencies**: how many company partners in the CNPJ register share each name or surname, plus IBGE Census rank, frequency, the state where the name is most common, the related spellings IBGE lists for it, how many women and men carry it and in which decade they were born. The README explains the IBGE names API, with sample calls; the data was fetched with the open-source client [ibge-nomes](https://github.com/CaiqueDourado/ibge-nomes).
- **A corpus of language-model output about names**: every row carries a meaning (names) or family history (surnames) written by text-davinci-002 or gpt-3.5, with the model named. Nobody reviewed them. Many are wrong in instructive ways: Araken "of Japanese origin" (it is Tupi), the city of Cerqueira César "in the north of Portugal" (it is in São Paulo), an invented 1573 genealogy for the Carrero family.

## Files

- `nomes.csv` / `nomes.parquet`: 46,840 given names, 31 columns.
- `sobrenomes.csv` / `sobrenomes.parquet`: 27,047 surnames, 11 columns.

Both tables have six keys for matching similar names: Portuguese Metaphone, OpenRefine fingerprint (with the 2023 bug documented), stems, character n-grams and a soft normalisation.

## Cleaning

Only rows with a usable text are published. Model refusals ("Não há um significado específico…", or any text that opens by saying no meaning is known), texts that switch to English, company words and codes were removed; sentence loops were cut; accent variants were merged. Surnames need 3 or more partners in the register; only counts are published, never a full name or a company.

Methodology, data quality report, data dictionary (EN and PT) and the build and validation scripts: **https://github.com/CaiqueDourado/nomes-e-sobrenomes-brasil**

## Related datasets

- [DedupKit](https://github.com/CaiqueDourado/DedupKit): matching library with the fixed fingerprint keyer and the Portuguese phonetic key
- [Municípios e Estados do Brasil](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/caiquedourado/municipios-e-estados-do-brasil)
- [Catálogo de produtos do e-commerce brasileiro](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/caiquedourado/catalogo-produtos-ecommerce-brasil)

resources.description: One row per given name (46,840): meaning written by GPT, CNPJ partner count, IBGE 2010 Census frequency and phonetic keys.

fields.name: name_id
fields.description: Id of the name in the 2023 database. Primary key.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Given name as published on the site, capitalised ("José", "Maria Júlia").

fields.name: meaning
fields.description: Meaning of the name in Portuguese, written by an OpenAI model in 2023. Not checked by a person: may be wrong or invented. Paragraphs separated by a line break.

fields.name: model
fields.description: Model that wrote the text: `text-davinci-002` or `gpt-3.5`.

fields.name: source
fields.description: Where the name came from: `cnpj` (first name of company partners in the CNPJ register), `search` (searches "significado do nome X"), `ibge_variant` (a spelling listed by the IBGE API for another name).

fields.name: cnpj_partners
fields.description: Number of company partners in the CNPJ register whose first name is this one (3 or more). Empty when the name did not come from the register.

fields.name: ibge_rank
fields.description: Rank of the name in the IBGE 2010 Census name list (1 = most common). Empty when the API had no data.

fields.name: ibge_frequency
fields.description: People with exactly this spelling in the 2010 Census, as returned by the IBGE API.

fields.name: ibge_percent
fields.description: Share of the population with the name, in percent.

fields.name: ibge_top_state
fields.description: State where the name is proportionally most common.

fields.name: ibge_top_state_per_100k
fields.description: People with the name per 100,000 inhabitants in that state.

fields.name: ibge_spellings
fields.description: Related spellings the IBGE API lists for this name, separated by `|` ("CAYQUE|KAIQUE|KAYQUE"). Each has its own frequency.

fields.name: ibge_female
fields.description: Women with this spelling in the 2010 Census (sum over decades of the v2 endpoint with `sexo=F`).

fields.name: ibge_male
fields.description: Men with this spelling in the 2010 Census (v2 endpoint with `sexo=M`).

fields.name: ibge_share_female
fields.description: `ibge_female / (ibge_female + ibge_male)`, 0 to 1.

fields.name: ibge_peak_decade
fields.description: Decade of birth with the most people with this spelling (`before_1930`, `1930s` … `2000s`).

fields.name: ibge_born_before_1930
fields.description: People with this spelling born before 1930, alive in 2010 (v2 endpoint).

fields.name: ibge_born_1930s
fields.description: People with this spelling born in the 1930s, alive in 2010 (v2 endpoint).

fields.name: ibge_born_1940s
fields.description: People with this spelling born in the 1940s, alive in 2010 (v2 endpoint).

fields.name: ibge_born_1950s
fields.description: People with this spelling born in the 1950s, alive in 2010 (v2 endpoint).

fields.name: ibge_born_1960s
fields.description: People with this spelling born in the 1960s, alive in 2010 (v2 endpoint).

fields.name: ibge_born_1970s
fields.description: People with this spelling born in the 1970s, alive in 2010 (v2 endpoint).

fields.name: ibge_born_1980s
fields.description: People with this spelling born in the 1980s, alive in 2010 (v2 endpoint).

fields.name: ibge_born_1990s
fields.description: People with this spelling born in the 1990s, alive in 2010 (v2 endpoint).

fields.name: ibge_born_2000s
fields.description: People with this spelling born in the 2000s, alive in 2010 (v2 endpoint).

fields.name: key_metaphone
fields.description: Phonetic key: Portuguese Metaphone (port of pt_metaphone, Várzea Paulista 2008). Names with the same key sound alike.

fields.name: key_fingerprint
fields.description: OpenRefine fingerprint key as computed in 2023. The port had a bug that keeps only every other word, so in names with several words it holds half of them (see data-quality).

fields.name: key_tokens
fields.description: Words reduced to their stem by the Brazilian stemmer (Lucene), in original order ("Lucas" → "luc").

fields.name: key_tokens_fingerprint
fields.description: The stems of `key_tokens`, sorted.

fields.name: key_ngram
fields.description: Character 2-gram fingerprint (OpenRefine variant): the letter pairs of the name, sorted, deduplicated and joined.

fields.name: key_soft
fields.description: Lower case, no accents, letters, digits and spaces only.
